verses.1: The LORD said to Moses, "Carve for yourself two stone tablets like the first ones, and I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, the ones you broke."
verses.2: Be ready by morning, and go up at dawn to Mount Sinai, and stand before me on the top of the mountain.
verses.3: No one must go up with you, and no one must be seen on the whole mountain. The sheep and the cattle must not graze near that mountain."
verses.4: Moses carved two stone tablets like the first ones. Moses rose early in the morning and went up to Mount Sinai, just as the LORD had commanded him, and in his hand he carried the two stone tablets.
verses.5: The LORD came down in a cloud and stood with him there. He called by the name of the LORD.
verses.6: The LORD passed by before him and called out, "The LORD, the LORD, a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love and faithfulness,
verses.7: who keeps steadfast love for thousands, who forgives iniquity and transgression and sin, but will by no means clear the guilty, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children and the children's children, to the third and the fourth generation."
verses.8: Moses quickly bowed to the ground and worshiped.
verses.9: He said, "If I have found favor in your sight, O Lord, please go in the midst of us, for this is a stiff-necked people, and you may forgive their iniquity and their sin, and you may give them possession."
verses.10: He said, "Behold, I am making a covenant before all your people. I will do wonders that have not been created in all the earth and among all the nations, and all the people among whom you are will see the work of the LORD, for it is awesome that I do with you."
verses.11: "Keep in mind what I command you today. Behold, I will drive out before you the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite.
verses.12: Be careful not to make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land into which you are going, for they will become a snare among you.
verses.13: You must tear down their altars, you must break down their pillars, and you must cut down their sacred trees.
verses.14: For you must not bow down to another god, for the LORD is a jealous God. His name is a jealous God.
verses.15: Be careful not to make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land, and they will seduce you to follow their gods, and they will sacrifice to their gods, and they will call you, and you will eat of their offerings.
verses.16: And you may take their daughters for your sons, and their daughters may seduce their sons after their gods, and their sons may seduce you after their gods."
verses.17: You must not make for yourself any molten gods.
verses.18: "You must keep the festival of unleavened bread. For seven days you must eat unleavened bread, just as I have commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of Abib, for in the month of Abib you came out of Egypt.
verses.19: Every firstborn male is mine, and every male from your livestock you must dedicate. Every firstborn of your ox and of your sheep.
verses.20: The firstborn of your donkey you must redeem with a lamb, and if you do not redeem it, you must break its neck. Every firstborn of your sons you must redeem, and none must appear before me empty-handed.
verses.21: For six days you must work, but on the seventh day you must rest. Even in plowing and in harvesting, you must rest."
verses.22: You must keep the Feast of Weeks by offering the firstfruits of your wheat harvest, and the Feast of Ingathering at the turning of the year.
verses.23: Three times a year all your males must appear before the LORD your God at the place he chooses: at the festival of Unleavened Bread, at the festival of Weeks, and at the festival of Ingathering.
verses.24: For I will drive out nations before you, and I will enlarge your borders, and no one will covet your land when you go up to appear before the LORD your God three times a year.
verses.25: You must not sacrifice to the LORD your God any offering of blood with leaven, and the offering of the Passover festival must not remain until morning.
verses.26: The firstfruits of your land you must bring to the house of the LORD your God. You must not boil a young goat in its mother's milk."
verses.27: The LORD said to Moses, "Write these words, for according to these words I have made a covenant with you and with Israel."
verses.28: Moses was there with the LORD forty days and forty nights. He did not eat bread, and he did not drink water. He wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the Ten Commandments.
verses.29: Now it happened when Moses came down from Mount Sinai, and the two stone tablets of the covenant were in his hand when he came down from the mountain, Moses did not know that the skin of his face had become radiant because the LORD had spoken with him.
verses.30: Aaron and all the Israelites saw Moses, and behold, the skin of his face was radiant, and they were afraid to come near him.
verses.31: Moses called to them, and Aaron and all the leaders of the congregation returned to him. Moses spoke to them.
verses.32: Afterward, all the Israelites came near, and Moses told them all that the LORD had spoken to him on Mount Sinai.
verses.33: When he had finished speaking to them, Moses put a veil over his face.
verses.34: Whenever Moses went in to speak with the LORD, he would remove the veil until he came out. When he came out and spoke to the Israelites what he had been commanded,
verses.35: the Israelites saw that Moses' face was radiant. Then Moses would put the veil back over his face until he went in to speak with the LORD.

notes:
Notes
- v. 7: "visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children" — this is a direct translation of the Hebrew phrase, preserving the meaning of intergenerational consequences.
- v. 30: "skin of his face was radiant" — the Hebrew uses "qaran," meaning "horned" or "radiant," which is commonly interpreted as "radiant" in modern translations.
- v. 33: "put a veil over his face" — the Hebrew term for "veil" is "masveh," which is rendered consistently as "veil" throughout the chapter.
raw:
[1] The LORD said to Moses, "Carve for yourself two stone tablets like the first ones, and I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, the ones you broke."

[2] Be ready by morning, and go up at dawn to Mount Sinai, and stand before me on the top of the mountain.

[3] No one must go up with you, and no one must be seen on the whole mountain. The sheep and the cattle must not graze near that mountain."

[4] Moses carved two stone tablets like the first ones. Moses rose early in the morning and went up to Mount Sinai, just as the LORD had commanded him, and in his hand he carried the two stone tablets.

[5] The LORD came down in a cloud and stood with him there. He called by the name of the LORD.

[6] The LORD passed by before him and called out, "The LORD, the LORD, a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love and faithfulness,

[7] who keeps steadfast love for thousands, who forgives iniquity and transgression and sin, but will by no means clear the guilty, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children and the children's children, to the third and the fourth generation."

[8] Moses quickly bowed to the ground and worshiped.

[9] He said, "If I have found favor in your sight, O Lord, please go in the midst of us, for this is a stiff-necked people, and you may forgive their iniquity and their sin, and you may give them possession."

[10] He said, "Behold, I am making a covenant before all your people. I will do wonders that have not been created in all the earth and among all the nations, and all the people among whom you are will see the work of the LORD, for it is awesome that I do with you."

[11] "Keep in mind what I command you today. Behold, I will drive out before you the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite.

[12] Be careful not to make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land into which you are going, for they will become a snare among you.

[13] You must tear down their altars, you must break down their pillars, and you must cut down their sacred trees.

[14] For you must not bow down to another god, for the LORD is a jealous God. His name is a jealous God.

[15] Be careful not to make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land, and they will seduce you to follow their gods, and they will sacrifice to their gods, and they will call you, and you will eat of their offerings.

[16] And you may take their daughters for your sons, and their daughters may seduce their sons after their gods, and their sons may seduce you after their gods."

[17] You must not make for yourself any molten gods.

[18] "You must keep the festival of unleavened bread. For seven days you must eat unleavened bread, just as I have commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of Abib, for in the month of Abib you came out of Egypt.

[19] Every firstborn male is mine, and every male from your livestock you must dedicate. Every firstborn of your ox and of your sheep.

[20] The firstborn of your donkey you must redeem with a lamb, and if you do not redeem it, you must break its neck. Every firstborn of your sons you must redeem, and none must appear before me empty-handed.

[21] For six days you must work, but on the seventh day you must rest. Even in plowing and in harvesting, you must rest."

[22] You must keep the Feast of Weeks by offering the firstfruits of your wheat harvest, and the Feast of Ingathering at the turning of the year.

[23] Three times a year all your males must appear before the LORD your God at the place he chooses: at the festival of Unleavened Bread, at the festival of Weeks, and at the festival of Ingathering.

[24] For I will drive out nations before you, and I will enlarge your borders, and no one will covet your land when you go up to appear before the LORD your God three times a year.

[25] You must not sacrifice to the LORD your God any offering of blood with leaven, and the offering of the Passover festival must not remain until morning.

[26] The firstfruits of your land you must bring to the house of the LORD your God. You must not boil a young goat in its mother's milk."

[27] The LORD said to Moses, "Write these words, for according to these words I have made a covenant with you and with Israel."

[28] Moses was there with the LORD forty days and forty nights. He did not eat bread, and he did not drink water. He wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the Ten Commandments.

[29] Now it happened when Moses came down from Mount Sinai, and the two stone tablets of the covenant were in his hand when he came down from the mountain, Moses did not know that the skin of his face had become radiant because the LORD had spoken with him.

[30] Aaron and all the Israelites saw Moses, and behold, the skin of his face was radiant, and they were afraid to come near him.

[31] Moses called to them, and Aaron and all the leaders of the congregation returned to him. Moses spoke to them.

[32] Afterward, all the Israelites came near, and Moses told them all that the LORD had spoken to him on Mount Sinai.

[33] When he had finished speaking to them, Moses put a veil over his face.

[34] Whenever Moses went in to speak with the LORD, he would remove the veil until he came out. When he came out and spoke to the Israelites what he had been commanded,

[35] the Israelites saw that Moses' face was radiant. Then Moses would put the veil back over his face until he went in to speak with the LORD.

Notes
- v. 7: "visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children" — this is a direct translation of the Hebrew phrase, preserving the meaning of intergenerational consequences.
- v. 30: "skin of his face was radiant" — the Hebrew uses "qaran," meaning "horned" or "radiant," which is commonly interpreted as "radiant" in modern translations.
- v. 33: "put a veil over his face" — the Hebrew term for "veil" is "masveh," which is rendered consistently as "veil" throughout the chapter.
